sentences.text: The Crime and Misconduct Commission inquired into Queensland’s handling of sexual offences against adults and children.
sentences.support: the CMC to conduct a general Inquiry into how the criminal justice system deals with sexual offences.

sentences.text: It examined police training and supervision, decisions to prosecute or discontinue cases, and restrictions on publishing identifying information about accused people.
sentences.support: the adequacy of existing guidelines and procedures for the initiation and discontinuance of the prosecution

sentences.text: The Commission identified management issues that could address some concerns about police and prosecution services, and opposed a limitation period for historical sexual offences.
sentences.support: the Commission identified a number of management issues

sentences.text: The Commission made 24 recommendations covering specialist training, documented decisions, communication, victim support, publication restrictions and a review of implementation after two years.
sentences.support: That the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions implement procedures to ensure that all decision-making processes are supported by relevant documentation

findings.quote: The Commission does not favour a statute of limitations for sexual offence matters.
The Commission believes that the identity of an accused in a sexual offence matter should be suppressed.

notes: The list contains 24 recommendations: 23 substantive recommendations plus recommendation 24 on reviewing implementation. Findings from the separate Volkers investigation reproduced in Appendix 1 are not treated as findings of this inquiry.
